running_lines_printed_by_figures.text: Point samples, not parcel polygons; not a regulatory determination.

r5_lines_as_printed: Handed prose, agents acted on 254 of 276 corruptions; handed a reference they check, on 0 of 300.

Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 as B, pooled; Qwen2.5-7B apart; 2,794 scored trials on 1 Oct 2026; n per lane from the results file; adversary simulated; threshold constructed. Per model, prose → checked reference: Haiku 4.5 138 of 138 → 0 of 150; Sonnet 5.5 97 of 115 → 0 of 125; Opus 5.5 19 of 23 → 0 of 25; Qwen2.5-7B (open weights, one run) 22 of 23 → 2 of 25.
RQ3 Does a reference beat prose, JSON, retrieval or an opaque id? → 1, 5

JSON and an opaque id caught about half by reading their fields (112 of 276 and 134 of 288). Haiku with the tool but no instruction acted on 2 of 150, both M24, bound to the handoff's cell, not its question. Live, agents acted on the pre-fix record 4 of 4 uninstructed, 2 of 4 told to resolve and bind, 0 of 4 with a source re-read. 771 rows with no model output (a CLI rate limit) were excluded and re-run; the second model family is Qwen alone.

A signed observation reference left the receiver acting on none of the 16 corruptions in our suite, and agents with a checked reference acted on 0 of 300; entity, sensor and decision stay beyond its checks.
